text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Symposium on business opportunities and international co-operation in Bosnia starts in Sarajevo. Bosnian Prime Minister, Hasan Muratovic, says $42 billion is needed to satisfy "urgent needs" in the field of reconstruction.
- The extension of OSCE's mandate in Bosnia until the end of next year requires Bosnian Serb president Biljana Plavsic's signature to take full effect, an OSCE spokesman says.

-European Community Humanitarian Office (ECHO) has donated 3 million German marks for the reconstruction of Gorazde in eastern Bosnia. The project will be carried out by Swedish Rescue Services Agency.
- Germany has approved $50 million German marks for the accommodation of 20,000 Bosnian refugees to be repatriated from Germany, a Bosnian official says.
- A new refugee camp opened Tuesday in the Federation village of Bukve, near Tesanj, with the assistance of Norwegian and Swedish humanitarian agencies.
